options.title: Le Panier des 4 Saisons
options.description: Hotel restaurant with fondue and other mountain dishes, rated highly by diners.
options.why: Well-reviewed fondue in Chamonix, a different spot from the planned dinner.

options.title: Le Fer à Cheval
options.description: Modern-styled alpine restaurant on Place du Poilu with a fondue complete of three cheeses and charcuterie.
options.why: Its cheese trio fondue suits a group sharing one pot.

options.title: La P'tite Verte
options.description: Lively, convivial spot known for its cheese fondue and a well-priced set menu.
options.why: A livelier, more budget-friendly option for a group dinner.

options.title: Aiguille du Midi cable car
options.description: Cable car up to a 3,842 m viewpoint with panoramic Mont Blanc views and a glass box on the terraces.
options.why: A top non-skier outing that needs no skiing and suits a clear day.
options.location: Chamonix town centre, cable car station a short walk from the centre

options.title: Montenvers train to Mer de Glace
options.description: Red rack train from central Chamonix up to the Mer de Glace glacier, with an ice cave to visit.
options.why: An easy half-day trip that gives glacier views without any skiing.
options.location: From Chamonix town centre up to the Mer de Glace

options.title: QC Terme Chamonix
options.description: Spa with an outdoor thermal pool and jacuzzis that look out to Mont Blanc.
options.why: A relaxing afternoon to rest after a day of walking or sightseeing.

options.title: Bar del Pla
options.description: Polished modern tapas by the Picasso Museum, a calmer sit-down option in El Born.
options.why: Reliable modern tapas for a relaxed first night in Barcelona.

options.title: Bormuth
options.description: A friendly, easygoing all-rounder in El Born serving classic tapas done well.
options.why: Good value and easygoing for a first tapas night without a crowd queue.

options.title: Sensi Tapas
options.description: A modern, creative tapas restaurant in the Gothic Quarter with vegetarian and vegan options and cocktails.
options.why: Open on Mondays from 17:45 and a good pick for a planned, sit-down evening out.

options.title: Museu Picasso
options.description: Art museum in the El Born area with a large collection tracing Picasso's early years in Barcelona.
options.why: A classic indoor art stop that works well if the rain sets in during the day.

options.title: Fundació Joan Miró
options.description: Modern art museum on Montjuïc hill with the largest collection of Miró's work, plus a rooftop terrace with city views.
options.why: Good for an afternoon of indoor art, with a view over the city if the weather clears.

options.title: CosmoCaixa Museum of Science
options.description: Science museum with hands-on exhibits and an immersive indoor rainforest.
options.why: Interactive and indoors, a good pick for a rainy day with a mixed group.

options.title: Café Bluebird
options.description: Popular café near the Aiguille du Midi cable car, known for a full English-style breakfast.
options.why: Good for a hearty pre-ski breakfast before the Feb 6 ski school.

options.title: Le Fournil Chamoniard
options.description: Bakery well reviewed for its bread and breakfast options.
options.why: Quick, affordable breakfast to grab on the way out for the day.

options.title: Omeletterie La Poële
options.description: Omelette-focused spot that also serves breakfast and brunch.
options.why: A sit-down option with plenty of egg dishes for a slower start.

options.title: Galerie Cafe des Aiguilles
options.description: Café with strong ratings and a mid-to-upper price range.
options.why: Highly rated breakfast stop for a treat before the morning lesson.

options.title: Bighorn Bistro
options.description: Bistro with a broad breakfast menu, including its silver spoon breakfast.
options.why: Filling sit-down breakfast with a wide menu for the whole group.

options.title: Poco Loco
options.description: Casual burger spot in Argentière, one of the cheapest sit-down-style options in the valley.
options.why: Well under the shown options and a relaxed, low-key dinner after a ski day.

options.title: La Roulotte
options.description: Italian pizza place known for affordable, well-regarded pizzas.
options.why: A cheap, quick dinner that is easy to fit around the group's schedule.

options.title: Casa Valerio
options.description: Town-centre pizza and fresh pasta restaurant, with pizzas starting around €20.
options.why: A mid-budget town-centre choice that is cheaper than the shown options and suits a casual group dinner.

options.title: Casa Valerio
options.description: Long-established Italian restaurant and pizzeria in the centre, with classic dishes and pizzas.
options.why: A well-known Italian choice for a group dinner in town, and reservations are available.
options.location: Tucked away in the Galerie Alpina near Place Mont Blanc, Chamonix

options.title: Joia by Pizzeria des Moulins
options.description: Authentic Italian pizzeria with thin-base pizzas, classic starters and desserts.
options.why: Popular Italian pizza spot that suits a relaxed group dinner in central Chamonix.

options.title: Restaurant Pizzeria Neapolis
options.description: Italian pizzeria and restaurant by the Arve with pizzas and pasta.
options.why: Good Italian option for a group dinner; bookings are taken by phone only, so call ahead.

options.title: Caelis
options.description: One-star Michelin restaurant with a weekday lunch menu.
options.why: A top-tier, special lunch that fits the higher-end, special ask.

options.title: Estimar
options.description: Seafood room on a side street in El Born, listed in the Michelin Guide.
options.why: A destination seafood lunch that feels like an occasion.

options.title: Cinc Sentits
options.description: Two-Michelin-star tasting menu restaurant in the Eixample.
options.why: The most special splurge of the three, with a tasting menu.

options.title: Le Monchu
options.description: Rustic Savoyard restaurant with a lively terrace over the town centre, known for cheese fondue and wood-fired raclette.
options.why: Another classic fondue-and-raclette room in the centre, close to the spirit of La Calèche.

options.title: Le Boccalatte
options.description: Popular local spot with traditional Savoyard fondue plus a steak and à la carte menu for non-cheese eaters.
options.why: Fondue with a wider menu, so the group isn't limited if someone skips cheese.

options.title: La P'tite Verte
options.description: Lively, convivial restaurant with authentic regional dishes and a popular cheese fondue.
options.why: A more casual, budget-friendly fondue night that suits a group.

options.title: Bar du Moulin
options.description: A cosy cellar bar on Rue des Moulins with warm wooden interiors and stone walls.
options.why: Cosy and central, a classic spot for an après-ski drink.

options.title: Le Cabanon Chamonix
options.description: A tiny stone-and-wood bar in the old town that fills with skiers after the slopes.
options.why: Atmospheric and cosy, with long happy hours for an early après-ski drink.
options.location: Rue des Moulins, Chamonix old quarter

options.title: Jekyll and Hyde
options.description: A cosy Irish pub over three floors with an open fire, gigs and quiz nights.
options.why: A warm, cosy pub with a fire, good for a relaxed evening drink after skiing.
